rites.name: Meramareno
rites.text: Meramareno is the concept of the first root-sound, the resonance by which the living roots of Venarirleth gathered into the first groves during the Singing. It is remembered in the Age of the first sovereign as the pattern that let scattered seedlings hold together and turn into kingdoms of growing wood.

rites.name: Osuvareno
rites.text: Osuvareno is the concept of resonance that moves through the Singing, the sounding in which the first roots of Venarirleth condense out of unformed tone. Its nature is held as a stable note that binds separate currents together, and during the Age of Sundering it is said to have been the chord that held landfall to the older bonds before they broke.

rites.name: Nuamae
rites.text: Nuamae is a rite of the Arcane realm in Venarirleth, performed in the Courts during the trials that shaped the first doors between worlds. Its flame is said to have sealed a gate in a single stroke, and the temples still count its hours in their liturgy.

rites.name: Thestoldock
rites.text: Thestoldock is a sealed ritual of the Courts, invoked when the council of flame convenes to bind a door between worlds shut. Its closing sends a shockwave through the temple vaults and silences the candles of every order in the region for a full night.

rites.name: Sileinys
rites.text: Sileinys is a rite held in the Courts of Venarirleth, where the council of arcane wardens bound the first door between worlds with a single chorus of answering runes. The sealing rang across the Sundering's fractured skies and left a lasting seam in the wards that still hums during storms.

rites.name: Jorernath
rites.text: Jorernath is a concept of Venarirleth, the quiet principle by which the makers plant the Weave during the Seeding, when slumbering powers are laid into the groves. It shapes the early growing kingdoms of the first sovereign's age, binding small wonders to the soil and the roots that hold them.

rites.name: Seiseth
rites.text: Seiseth is a concept in Venarirleth, the principle by which the makers plant the Weave so that quiet powers may sleep beneath the world. In the Holy Age of flame, temples and orders, its teaching is kept by sealed orders who tend the hidden threads.

rites.name: Cruraste
rites.text: Cruraste is the concept of a binding oath, held in the Arcane Realm of Venarirleth during the Holy Age, when the Pact was sworn over broken worlds. Its adherents treat it as a flame that keeps promises alive across the Shards.

rites.name: Grimogun
rites.text: Grimogun is the concept of binding oaths made in Venarirleth's Arcane Realm during the Fall, when worlds broke apart and the Pact was sworn. It is said to be the will that holds a sworn word against the drift of shattered ground. Its power is felt most where old bonds gave way to landfall.

rites.name: Tarnarduste
rites.text: Tarnarduste is the concept of the wall as a binding will, a principle that the Walled Age of Venarirleth held as sacred for centuries. Its orders and churches taught that a held line is a promise kept, and its first crossings were recorded as the moment that promise first broke.

rites.name: Fenoldeld
rites.text: Fenoldeld is a binding concept of Venarirleth's Arcane Realm, held in the Walled Age as the principle that a boundary kept long enough becomes a power of its own. Its orders, shaped during the reign of the first sovereign, taught growing kingdoms to raise hedges and wards that outlived the hands that set them.

rites.name: Ryenallae
rites.text: Ryenallae is a silver-thread rite of the Venarirleth lantern-courts, in which a petitioner ties a borrowed name to their own pulse so that a distant ally may be called across the veil for a single night. The bond frays the caller's spirit and leaves a faint humming scar on whoever answers.

rites.name: Nistesum
rites.text: Nistesum is the concept of the branching of endings in Venarirleth, the moment when one future divides into three and the Library must decide where each thread is shelved. It is not a being but a principle that the Arcane Realm of the Three Futures keeps in careful balance.

rites.name: Anasatanum
rites.text: Anasatanum is the concept of a sealed branching of fate, a single unopened page the Library keeps between futures that have not yet been chosen. In the Age of the first sovereign it was whispered among the groves as the reason a seed might bloom in one season and wither in another.

rites.name: Sathyuvsith
rites.text: Sathyuvsith is a concept born in the Three Futures of Venarirleth, a notion that the ending branches and the Library shelves each outcome as its own thread. It was named during the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke the old bonds between peoples and their stories.
